question: A 23-year-old man comes to the physician for frequent and painful urination. He has also had progressive painful swelling of his right knee over the past week. He is sexually active with two female partners and uses condoms inconsistently. His mother has an autoimmune disease that involves a malar rash. Examination shows conjunctivitis bilaterally. The right knee is warm, erythematous, and tender to touch; range of motion is limited. Laboratory studies show an erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 62 mm/h. Urinalysis shows WBCs. Further evaluation of this patient is most likely to reveal which of the following?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "23-year-old man with frequent painful urination" -> "possible urinary tract infection or sexually transmitted infection" -> "progressive painful swelling of right knee" -> "suggestive of inflammatory arthritis" -> "bilateral conjunctivitis present" -> "possible systemic condition" -> "family history of autoimmune disease" -> "possible lupus erythematosus" -> "likely positive anti-dsDNA antibodies" -> 85%

CHAIN: "23-year-old man with painful urination and knee swelling" -> "symptoms suggestive of reactive arthritis" -> "recent sexual activity with inconsistent condom use" -> "possible sexually transmitted infection" -> "bilateral conjunctivitis indicates systemic involvement" -> "family history of autoimmune disease" -> "possible association with HLA-B27" -> "but less likely than anti-dsDNA in this context" -> 70%

CHAIN: "23-year-old man with joint swelling and urination issues" -> "elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate indicates inflammation" -> "conjunctivitis and joint symptoms suggest systemic disease" -> "family history of autoimmune disease" -> "anti-dsDNA antibodies are specific for lupus" -> "more likely than chondrocalcinosis or HLA-B27" -> 90%

CHAIN: "23-year-old man with knee swelling and urination problems" -> "possible inflammatory arthritis due to infection" -> "bilateral conjunctivitis suggests systemic involvement" -> "family history of autoimmune disease" -> "anti-dsDNA antibodies are a common finding in lupus" -> "less likely to be chondrocalcinosis or HLA-B27" -> 80%
analysis: The patient's symptoms, including painful urination, swollen knee, conjunctivitis, and a family history of autoimmune disease (suggestive of lupus), point towards a possible autoimmune condition. The presence of a malar rash in the mother raises suspicion for systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). The elevated ESR and urinalysis showing WBCs suggest an inflammatory process, possibly related to an autoimmune disease. The most relevant laboratory finding that would support a diagnosis of SLE in this context would be positive anti-dsDNA antibodies, which are specific for lupus. Therefore, further evaluation is most likely to reveal positive anti-dsDNA antibodies.
